item: row 341: key-file reads are bounded, never block and read only a regular file
key_paths: src/custody/keyfile.py; src/reporting/evidence.py; src/api/custody.py; tests/test_zz_dev_null_is_left_alone.py; tests/test_key_reads_bounded_row341.py; tests/test_evidence_key_wrap.py
summary: a FIFO put at the evidence key's name hung the export review (existing_public_key_hex read it with an unbounded read_bytes) and every own-key check; a link to /dev/zero read forever. The shared key reader keyfile.read_once (behind read_settled, used by the evidence key, the custody signer and the review) now opens with O_NONBLOCK, refuses anything fstat does not call a regular file and stops one byte past MAX_KEY_FILE_BYTES (64 KiB; the largest key written, a wrapped ML-DSA-65 pair, is 6028 bytes), raising KeyFileNotReadable (an OSError, never FileNotFoundError, so no loader makes a key over it); the review reads through it, so each reads as 'own key could not be read' (R795 R4), fail closed, no hang. Links are still followed (test_evidence_key_wrap pins a linked key loading); the checks apply to what the link names. The Custody status read now answers such a key as unreadable instead of a 500 (security read). Plan-ruled plain correctness.
